title: TA9-02176
frame:
Forum: Refugee Protection Division (first-instance tribunal).
Parties: the claimant and the Minister; names are redacted.
Decision under review: none; this is the first-instance decision.
How the layers nest here: The member of the tribunal is the author (layer 1). The claimant and the Minister make submissions to the member (layer 2). There is no earlier decision-maker unless the reasons describe a prior decision (layer 3). Testimony and documents are layer 5.

paragraphs.text: The claimant, XXXXX XXXXX (age 20), is a male from the Czech Republic. He claims refugee protection pursuant to ss. 96 and 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act1 (IRPA).

The claimant did not have counsel at the hearing. The claimant confirmed that he had been given adequate time to retain a lawyer. He stated that he wished to proceed with the hearing. He acknowledged that he had been given disclosure of documents from the Refugee Protection Division. He confirmed that he had been instructed as to the procedure and suggested evidence he should have for the hearing. The hearing proceeded after questioning the claimant on his ability to proceed without counsel and reviewing with him the relevant sections of the IRPA when the issues were discussed.
The claimant states that he is of Roma ethnicity. He claims that he has been persecuted in the Czech Republic because of his ethnicity.

He alleges that skinheads have attacked him many times. He maintains that the most serious incident occurred in XXXXX 2008, when he was taking a bus to see some friends. He says there was a group of skinheads on the bus who started to verbally insult him. He maintains that after about two minutes of verbal abuse they attacked him physically. He states that the bus driver stopped the bus and left and the other people in the bus did not do anything. He states that he woke up outside of the bus near a bus stop. He states that the police did not do anything about the assault and one of his friends who is a nurse, helped him with his injuries.
I find that the claimant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection. ANALYSIS Identity
The claimant's oral testimony and the supporting documentation filed,2 establish his identity as a national of the Czech Republic. Convention Refugee
The determinative issue is whether there is a serious possibility that the claimant will be persecuted, if he returns to the Czech Republic by reason of his Roma ethnicity.
I find that the claimant does not have a well-founded fear of persecution, if he should return to the Czech Republic. Discrimination vs. Persecution

Does the discrimination suffered by this claimant amount to persecution when considered singularly or cumulatively? To be considered persecution, the mistreatment suffered or anticipated must be serious. In order to determine whether a particular mistreatment would qualify as "serious", one must examine what interest of the claimant might be harmed; and to what extent the subsistence, enjoyment, expression or exercise of that interest might be compromised. "Persecution", for example, undefined in the Convention, has been ascribed the meaning of sustained or systemic violation of basic human rights demonstrative of a failure of state protection.3 In the case of Chan,4 La Forest J. (in dissent) reiterated that the essential question is whether the persecution alleged by the claimant threatens his or her basic human rights in a fundamental way.

In his testimony, the claimant said that he went to elementary school with a mixture of Czech and Roma people. He states that he was verbally insulted at school and if he was unable to grasp something in class the teacher called him a "stupid gypsy." He says that his mother complained to the principal two or three times about the treatment that he received. He maintains that he was still treated badly in school. He states that he wanted to change schools but the only option was to attend a school for special needs individuals. He says that there were not many opportunities if a person attended the school. He states that he went to a vocational school and studied to be a brick layer. He maintains that vocational school was his only option and he believes that he would not be admitted to another school even if he had attained high marks. He says that when it came time to fill out forms for high school, the teacher did not even give him the forms because she told him that he did not have the chance to get into those schools.

He says that after XXXXX school he obtained the job working in a XXXXX and he stayed there for approximately 3 months. He states that while he worked there something was lost in the warehouse and he was blamed because he was a gypsy. XXXXX states that he was fired from his job. He says he had four different jobs working as a brick XXXXX and a XXXXX XXXXX. He maintains that he was always given the worst jobs but he always did his best.

He alleges that he was attacked in XXXXX 2008 by skinheads when he was shopping with his mother. He says that he and his mother were crossing a street and he was carrying some bags. A group of four or five skinheads started verbally insulting them and then attacked him and his mother. He states that his mother called an ambulance and he was in the hospital for 24 hours. He said that the doctor checked him out, put a bandage on his head and sent him home. He was asked if he had any medical report as a result of this incident. He said that he had the report in the Czech Republic but he forgot to bring it to Canada. He then said that he tried to get the report for the hearing but his mother could not find it. He states that he went to the police to report the incident four days later but they told him that because he had no witnesses they could not do anything. He testified that his mother tried to go to some police superiors about the matter but she was unsuccessful. He testified that he was subjected to other attacks by skinheads but they were not as serious as the incident with him and his mother. He says that he went to the police several times because of the attacks and sometimes they would write reports but there was no follow-up. He said that it was difficult to get the police reports for this hearing.

It was pointed out to the claimant that in his Personal Information Form5 (PIF) narrative, he stated that the most serious attack which he suffered, occurred on a bus when he went to meet a group of friends. In his testimony he stated that the most serious attack occurred when he went shopping with his mother. When he was asked for an explanation as to this inconsistency, he said he did not know why he did not tell the Board about the attack on the bus. If the claimant had been attacked in either of these incidents he would have remembered them and related both of them in his testimony and in his PIF narrative. The claimant was unable to provide a medical report of either incident. He said that he forgot a medical report when he left the Czech Republic and he said that his mother could not find it when he asked her for it. I do not accept this explanation. I conclude that he did not suffer a serious attack by skinheads in the Czech Republic.

The claimant may have suffered discrimination while he lived in the Czech Republic because of his Roma ethnicity. However, I conclude from the examples given by the claimant that there is no persuasive evidence of sustained or systemic violation of basic human rights demonstrative of a failure of state protection.

The discrimination claimed in this matter does not rise to the level of persecution. Therefore, I conclude that the claimant does not have a well-founded fear of persecution and there is no serious possibility that he will be persecuted, if he returns to the Czech Republic. There is also no persuasive evidence that, on a balance of probabilities, he is at risk to his life or at risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment or torture, if he returns to the Czech Republic.

Having considered all of the evidence, I find that the claimant is not a Convention refugee or a person in need of protection. The Refugee Protection Division therefore, rejects the claim for refugee protection.
